speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with fever and abdominal tenderness after giving birth; have you experienced chills, headache, or visual changes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given the uterine tenderness, urinary symptoms, and decreased bowel sounds, are you currently experiencing pain when urinating or passing stool? Also, please tell me the exact temperature you measured and how long the fever has persisted.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Urinalysis, Urine_Culture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis with secondary urinary retention.

I strongly disagree with the suggestion of iron deficiency anemia as the primary cause of your fever and acute abdominal tenderness; your symptoms point to an infection of the uterine lining. We need to see the results of the blood work and urinalysis I ordered to confirm the infection and rule out other causes. Once those results are available, we will proceed with appropriate antibiotic treatment.
